structural: The structural obligations are the three declarations in the requirement's Rust block, plus the clause that loaded contents retain the scheme. The rest of the text is behavior.

1. Trait method. The text says `fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;` on `OutlineLang` and that "Each language supplies the scheme". The trait declaration `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#trait[OutlineLang]/fn[fingerprint_scheme]` has that signature and no default body, so every language must supply the scheme. An alternative that put the scheme in a provider-side constant instead of this method would violate the clause. The root covers this.

2. Retained scheme. The text says "Loaded contents retain the scheme used to compute their hashes". `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#struct[Snapshot]` has a `scheme: String` field. `OutlineContent::prepare` fills it from the scheme passed in. `parse_with` passes `language.fingerprint_scheme()`, and `parse_source` passes the profile's scheme. A design that recomputed the scheme from the language name on each call would not retain it, so the field is a real structural obligation. The root covers it.

3. Content accessor. The text says `impl OutlineContent { pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str; }`. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#impl[OutlineContent]/fn[fingerprint_scheme]` returns `&self.snapshot.scheme`, which matches the signature and the retained value. The root covers it.

The remaining code is behavior or is reached from these roots:
- The `language!` macro in `languages/mod.rs` implements the trait method by returning `$profile.fingerprint_scheme`.
- The per-language `Profile` statics each set a versioned scheme string, for example `rust-structural-v1` and `typescript-structural-v2`.
- `prepare` and `parse_with` do the copying.

These are discretionary ways to supply and store the value. The trait signature already forces a supply, and `Snapshot` already forces retention. Whether a scheme changes when the hash rules change is a behavioral obligation, and the tests cover it. No further implementation root is needed.

behavioral: The obligations are: (a) each language supplies a scheme through `OutlineLang::fingerprint_scheme`, (b) a rule change uses a different scheme, and an update that preserves the calculation may keep it, and (c) loaded contents retain the scheme used for their hashes.

(a) and (c) are covered by `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme]`.
- `CustomLanguage` returns its configuration string as the scheme.
- The test builds contents with `from_source_with` and `from_path_with`.
- It checks that the root `fingerprint().scheme` is `custom-v2:own-v1`.
- It drops the language, its clone and the configuration `Arc`, then asserts `supplied.fingerprint_scheme() == "custom-v2"`. That shows the scheme is retained by the contents and not read back from the language.
- It selects an item from the contents after the drop. `fingerprint()` is built from the retained scheme (confirmed in `NodeContents::fingerprint`), and the loaded and supplied selections have equal fingerprints.

For (b), the same test builds a `custom-v3` language that produces the same `structural_hash` as `custom-v2`. It asserts that the fingerprints differ, so the scheme is what distinguishes the two rule versions. Retaining a scheme when the calculation is unchanged is a permission (MAY) and needs no test. The same scheme with the same hash gives equal fingerprints, which the loaded-versus-selected comparison covers.

Built-in language inference is covered by `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[file_constructors_infer_the_language_and_return_addressed_contents]`. It asserts `root.fingerprint_scheme() == "rust-structural-v1"` for contents loaded with `from_path`. Other tests also assert the scheme, for example in `contracts.rs` and `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits`.

The tests do not assert `selected.fingerprint_scheme()` directly or call `language.fingerprint_scheme()` directly. The scheme is a single value held in the shared snapshot, and the selected item's `fingerprint().scheme` and the fingerprint comparisons exercise it. I do not consider that a gap.
